qwen_chat.w: This section only provides definitions for terms used in the Act, specifically identifying which congressional committees are considered 'appropriate.' It does not require or recommend any participation, consultation, or coordination with outside parties. Additionally, Congress is part of the federal government, so interactions with it do not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: (1) Appropriate congressional committees.—The term “appropriate congressional committees” means— (A) the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate; (B) the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; (C) the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate; (D) the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives; (E) the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives; and (F) the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that defining "appropriate congressional committees" implies that these committees will participate in the decision-making process described elsewhere in the Act. However, this section is purely definitional. It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or advisory role for these committees within this specific text. Furthermore, Congress is considered "inside" the federal government, so even if it did mandate consultation, it would likely be "No" under the definition (reports to Congress are explicitly excluded). But primarily, this section just defines terms.
